---
title: "Environmental Chemistry"
---

How do molecular properties and reactions determine what happens to substances
in air, water, and soil? This course connects equilibrium, reaction rates,
partitioning, and chemical balances to transport and potential exposure.

Start with [environmental amounts and balances](environmental-systems/notes.qmd),
or use the [course content](overview.qmd) to find a topic. The sequence follows
atmosphere, water, soils, and contaminants, with particular depth in aquatic
chemistry. The [glossary](glossary.qmd) links common terms to their explanations.

## Work through a unit

Read the chemical question and learning goals. Use the notes with the short
lecture, then try the exercises before opening their hints and worked solutions.
State units, assumptions, and the system boundary in every calculation. Explain
what a numerical answer means chemically and what it cannot establish.

Three short R activities reuse table handling, plotting, and reproducible reports
from introductory computing. Their [downloads](overview.qmd#three-supporting-computing-activities)
include starting code and a report template. Hand calculations provide a check
before the code is used.

## Explore chemical predictions

The interactive demos, listed in orange under each week in the sidebar, let you vary deposition,
carbon inventories, ligand conditions, sorption, transformation, and catchment
neutralisation. Each has a hand-check reference and questions that connect the
plot to a chemical balance.

## Connect the chemical systems

The recurring constructed catchment links deposition, soil reactions, and water
alkalinity. A second constructed sediment case links oxygen depletion, iron,
and phosphorus. The [integrated case](integrated-case/notes.qmd) brings these
mechanisms and their evidence together in a short chemical argument.

These materials form a first teaching draft. The working reference is vanLoon
and Duffy, *Environmental Chemistry: A Global Perspective*, fourth edition.
